feature-17398941.text:
Feature: resilient recipe fetching, with an optional proxy and an optional FlareSolverr.

Many recipe sites sit behind bot protection (Cloudflare and similar). Today a URL import only rotates browser impersonations on a plain 403. A 429 or 503, a response flagged with a cf-mitigated header, or a 200 "just a moment" interstitial is either taken as the page or ends the import. Image downloads always use a single impersonation. Operators also have no way to send scraping through a proxy with a better IP reputation, or through a self-hosted FlareSolverr instance that solves challenges in a real browser.

Expected:

Settings
1. AppSettings (read from the environment like the other settings) gets four new settings:
   - SCRAPER_PROXY_URL: an optional string, default None.
   - SCRAPER_PROXY_MODE: a ScraperProxyMode, default always. ScraperProxyMode is a new string enum in the settings module (the one that defines AppSettings). Its members are always ("always") and fallback ("fallback"), and any unrecognised value falls back to always.
   - SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL: an optional string, default None.
   - SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT: an int number of seconds, default 60.
2. SCRAPER_PROXY_URL and SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL are checked when settings load:
   - Unset gives None.
   - A value that is set must parse as a URL with both a scheme and a host. Otherwise get_app_settings() raises pydantic's ValidationError. Rejected: "flaresolverr:8191", "192.168.1.5:8191", "just-a-hostname".
   - Accepted values are kept exactly as given, as plain strings: "http://flaresolverr:8191", "https://fs.example.com:8191/", "http://user:pass@host:8080" and "socks5://host:1080". Any scheme is fine.
   The existing settings behave as before.

New fetch module
3. Add a submodule named fetch to the safehttp package (the package that holds AsyncSafeTransport). It provides:
   - BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS: the browser impersonations to rotate through. This is today's chrome, firefox, safari and edge list, now owned here.
   - ScraperProxyMode, importable as fetch.ScraperProxyMode.
   - is_challenge_status(status_code), returning a real bool. It is True for 503 and for every 4xx except 404 and 410, and False for everything else. So 400, 401, 402, 403, 406, 429, 451 and 503 are True; 200, 301, 404, 410, 500, 502 and 504 are False.
   - headers_indicate_challenge(headers): True when the httpx.Headers carry a cf-mitigated header (any value; the header name is case-insensitive). It is False otherwise, for example with only server: cloudflare or with no headers at all.
   - body_indicates_challenge(content): True when the first _CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE bytes of the body contain a known anti-bot marker, compared case-insensitively. _CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE is a module-level int, for example 4096.
     - The markers include __cf_chl, cf-browser-verification and /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform. You may add other vendor-specific ones, for example datadome.
     - Ordinary page text such as "A normal recipe for cookies" does not match.
     - A marker that only appears after the sampled window is not detected.
   - FetchResult, a dataclass built positionally as FetchResult(content, status_code, url, headers, encoding). The field types are bytes, int, str, httpx.Headers, and str or None.
     - Its text property decodes content with encoding, replacing bad bytes.
     - When encoding is None or an unknown name (for example "not-real"), text falls back to a default decode instead of raising.
     - FetchResult(b"h\xc3\xa9llo", 200, "http://x", httpx.Headers(), "utf-8").text is "héllo".
   - async resilient_fetch(url, *, method="GET", timeout=15, allow_flaresolverr=True), returning a FetchResult or None. Its behaviour is described below.
4. resilient_fetch works through these module-level names, and only these:
   - _build_transport(impersonate, proxy=None) builds the transport for one attempt. That is an AsyncSafeTransport with that impersonation, default browser headers, SSL verification off as today, and routed through proxy when one is given. Every attempt calls it exactly once, with that attempt's impersonation and its proxy (None for a direct attempt).
   - Each attempt opens its own client through the module-level name AsyncClient (httpx's), passing that transport.
     - It sends the request with client.stream(method, url, ...) used as an async context manager.
     - From the response it reads only status_code, headers, encoding and url, and it reads the body with aiter_bytes().
     - Nothing else on the client or the response is used (no get, head or aread).
   - Settings come from calling the module-level name get_app_settings() on every fetch. Only SCRAPER_PROXY_URL, SCRAPER_PROXY_MODE, SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL and SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT are read from it.
   - Waits use asyncio.sleep(seconds), with asyncio imported by the module.
   - FlareSolverr is called as flaresolverr.solve(...) through the flaresolverr submodule. fetch exposes that submodule as its attribute fetch.flaresolverr, and solve is looked up at call time.

resilient_fetch behaviour
5. Rotation. It tries the impersonations one attempt each (shuffling the order is fine) and returns the first success.
   - A blocked response moves on to the next impersonation. A response is blocked when is_challenge_status or headers_indicate_challenge is true. When the body is read, it is also blocked when body_indicates_challenge is true. So a 200 interstitial followed by a real 200 page returns the real page after 2 attempts.
   - Any other status of 400 or more (404, 410, 500 and so on) is a hard error. The fetch stops at once, after that single attempt, and returns None. A hard error never escalates to the proxy or to FlareSolverr.
   - For GET, the body is read up to the timeout as today. Reading for longer raises ForceTimeoutException (it stays importable where the recipe routes import it today).
   - A HEAD request never reads the body. A HEAD response that is not blocked returns a FetchResult with content b"", even when the server sent a body that looks like a challenge.
   - After a blocked 429 or 503, if another attempt follows, it waits first.
     - When Retry-After is a number of seconds, it waits at least that long. For example, Retry-After: 2 means one asyncio.sleep call with at least 2.0.
     - Without a usable Retry-After, it waits about a second.
     - The wait is capped at a few seconds, plus a little random jitter.
   - No other block waits. A 403 moves on with no sleep at all.
   - The whole fetch, attempts and waits together, has an overall budget of about 45 seconds.
   - If every impersonation is blocked and nothing escalates, the result is None after exactly len(BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS) attempts.
6. Proxy. With no SCRAPER_PROXY_URL, every attempt gets proxy None. With a proxy set, the mode decides:
   - Mode always: every attempt goes through the proxy, including the first (even when it succeeds). If they are all blocked, there is no second rotation: exactly len(BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS) attempts, all proxied.
   - Mode fallback: first a full direct rotation (proxy None). Only when every direct attempt was blocked does a second rotation run through the proxy, so the attempt after the last direct one uses the proxy URL. A hard error never escalates to the proxy.
7. FlareSolverr is the last resort. It is used only when all of these hold: the fetch is still blocked after the steps above, SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL is set, the method reads a body (not HEAD), and allow_flaresolverr is true.
   - It then calls flaresolverr.solve(SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL, url, SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT) once, positionally, for example ("http://flaresolverr:8191", "https://x/r", 60).
   - If solve returns a solution, resilient_fetch returns a FetchResult built from it: the content is the solution's html encoded as UTF-8, the encoding is "utf-8", status_code and url come from the solution, and the headers give a text/html content type. Its .text equals the solved HTML.
   - If solve returns None, resilient_fetch returns None.
   - solve is never called after a hard error (404), when the URL is unset, for HEAD, or with allow_flaresolverr=False.

New flaresolverr module
8. Add a submodule named flaresolverr to the same package. It imports httpx and provides:
   - FlareSolverrSolution, a dataclass with html, status_code and url, plus cookies (default an empty list) and user_agent (default ""). It can be built with only html, status_code and url as keywords.
   - async solve(base_url, url, timeout), returning a FlareSolverrSolution or None.
9. How solve sends its request:
   - It POSTs to base_url with any trailing slash removed plus "/v1". So "http://flaresolverr:8191/" gives "http://flaresolverr:8191/v1".
   - The JSON payload has cmd "request.get", url set to the page URL, and maxTimeout set to timeout in milliseconds (30 gives 30000).
   - It creates its client as httpx.AsyncClient(...), looked up on the httpx module at call time, and uses it as an async context manager. The HTTP timeout goes on the client and should be somewhat longer than timeout.
   - It calls client.post(endpoint, json=payload) with no other arguments. From the response it uses only status_code and json().
10. What solve returns:
   - It returns a solution only for HTTP 200 with JSON whose status is "ok" and whose solution.response is non-empty.
   - The solution's fields are filled from the JSON: html from solution.response, status_code from solution.status (default 200), url from solution.url (default the requested url), cookies from solution.cookies (default []), and user_agent from solution.userAgent (default "").
   - It returns None, and never raises, in every other case: the request raises (for example httpx.ConnectError), the HTTP status is not 200 (for example 500), json() raises (the body is not JSON), status is not "ok" (for example {"status": "error", "message": ...}), or solution.response is empty.

Use it
11. URL imports fetch the recipe page, and download its image, through resilient_fetch so that the proxy applies to both.
   - FlareSolverr applies to the page only: image downloads pass allow_flaresolverr=False.
   - The size probe that picks the largest of several image URLs uses method="HEAD".
   - A page that cannot be fetched still scrapes as an empty string, and an image that cannot be fetched is skipped, as today.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

feature-36d716a4.text:
Feature: structured recipe times, stored as seconds next to the free text.

Recipe total, prep and cook times are only free text today. Imports turn a schema.org duration such as "PT1H30M" into English words ("1 hour 30 minutes", or "none" for a zero time) whatever the user's language, migrations from other apps write their own English, and the schema.org JSON Mealie serves for a recipe page repeats that text where schema.org expects ISO 8601 durations. Users want real durations that can be localized and relied on, while keeping free text for what is not a duration ("overnight", "about an hour").

Expected:

1. Recipe schema and API
- RecipeSummary (so also Recipe and every response that embeds it) gets total_time_seconds, prep_time_seconds and perform_time_seconds (JSON totalTimeSeconds, prepTimeSeconds, performTimeSeconds): optional whole seconds, default null, from 0 to 2147483647 (the Postgres INTEGER max). None, 0, 5400 and 2147483647 are kept as given; -1 and 2147483648 fail validation (building a RecipeSummary raises pydantic's ValidationError, which is a ValueError).
- The text fields total_time, prep_time, cook_time and perform_time stay, with their current coercion (None stays None, "" stays "", 10 gives "10", 2.25 gives "2.25"). There is no structured cook_time: perform_time_seconds is the structured cook time. Wherever this feature turns a time into seconds, that time's text becomes null; text is kept only for what is not a duration.
- The API stores and returns the seconds and text a client sends. Saving a recipe never reinterprets its text (a PUT with "totalTime": "PT25M" keeps that text), and a zip export and re-import keeps all four text fields.

2. Database and Alembic migration
- The recipes table gets three nullable INTEGER columns, total_time_seconds, prep_time_seconds and perform_time_seconds, mapped on RecipeModel, so recipes persist and return the new fields.
- A new Alembic migration adds them: revision id 27621d27c7e1, down revision 3527efeeec34 (the current head), message "add structured recipe times", create date 2026-09-24 13:16:56. Name its file with the project's migration file template (file_template in alembic.ini), so the name contains the revision id and sorts after every existing migration (tests/unit_tests/test_alembic.py checks that the sorted files chain). Tests find it with ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob("*27621d27c7e1*.py"), load it standalone with import_file from tests/utils/alembic_reader.py, and call its functions while the test module is imported.
- Upgrade adds the columns, then converts the existing text in total_time, prep_time and perform_time (cook_time is left alone): when parse_seconds (below) reads a text, its seconds are stored and the text is set to NULL; otherwise, when is_empty_time is true for it (the "none" the scraper used to write for a zero time), the text is set to NULL; anything else stays exactly as it was. Downgrade first writes format_seconds(seconds) into each of those text fields that is NULL while its seconds are set, then drops the three columns.
- The migration module itself defines these functions, which tests call directly. The parsing lives in the migration and does not use the scraper code, so later scraper changes cannot change what the migration did.
  - load_unit_words(locales_dir=<the backend translations folder, mealie/lang/messages>) returns a dict from unit word to unit name. It reads every *.json file in the folder and, from its "datetime" object, the entries "day", "hour", "minute" and "second" (each like "hour|hours"). Each entry is split on "|", every word is stripped and casefolded, and empty words are skipped. Files that cannot be read, are not valid JSON or are not a JSON object are skipped. A word listed under two different units (in one file or across files) is ambiguous and must not appear in the result at all. Example: aa-AA.json {"datetime": {"hour": "tick|ticks", "minute": "min"}}, bb-BB.json {"datetime": {"second": "tick|tock"}} and broken.json containing "{" give exactly {"ticks": "hour", "min": "minute", "tock": "second"}.
  - build_component_pattern(unit_words) builds, from those words, the matcher for one "<number><unit word>" component (a compiled regular expression). Tests build it once and only pass it to parse_seconds.
  - parse_seconds(value, unit_words, pattern) returns the duration in whole seconds, or None unless the entire value reads as one clear duration:
    a. None, "" and whitespace only give None; surrounding whitespace is ignored.
    b. A bare number (digits, optionally a dot and more digits; no sign, no comma) is minutes: "30" gives 1800, "1.5" gives 90.
    c. A value starting with "P" or "p" is read only as an ISO 8601 duration, case-insensitively: "PT15M" 900, "PT1H30M" 5400, "pt1h" 3600, "P1DT2H" 93600, "PT90S" 90. Years and months have no fixed length, so "P1M" and "P1Y" give None, and "PTXM" (invalid) gives None.
    d. Anything else must consist entirely of one or more components, each a number as in (b) followed by a unit word from unit_words, matched case-insensitively. The space between number and word, and between components, is optional, but a word must be followed by whitespace, a digit or the end of the text. Units must come largest first (day, hour, minute, second), each at most once. Read: "1 hour 30 minutes" 5400, "1 Hour" 3600, "2 days 4 hours" 187200, "45 seconds" 45, "1 Stunde 30 Minuten" 5400, "2 heures 15 minutes" 8100, "1 時間 30 分" 5400, "1時間30分" 5400, "1.5 hours" 5400, "  20 minutes  " 1200. None for "about 30 minutes", "30 minutes, plus overnight", "1 hour and 30 minutes", "1 hour, 30 minutes", "Overnight", "none", "30 minutes 1 hour" (out of order), "10 minutes 5 minutes" (repeated), and "30 mins" and "1 hr" (not words from the translations).
    e. In every case the total must be a whole number of seconds (nothing is rounded), above 0 and at most 2147483647, otherwise None: "0", "PT0M" and "0 minutes" (zero), "PT0.5S" and "0.001" (not whole seconds), "P30000D" (too large).
  - is_empty_time(value) returns a real bool: True when the value, stripped and casefolded, is exactly "none" ("none", " None "), and False for None, "", "none needed" and "30 minutes".
  - format_seconds(seconds) returns English text in the scraper's old shape: days, hours, minutes and seconds, zero parts left out, singular for 1, separated by single spaces. 60 gives "1 minute", 5400 "1 hour 30 minutes", 93690 "1 day 2 hours 1 minute 30 seconds".

3. Cleaning (the scraper's cleaner module, the one with clean, clean_time and pretty_print_timedelta; tests call these as cleaner.<name>)
- A new function clean_duration(time_entry) returns whole seconds when the entry is a structured duration, and None for anything that should stay text:
  - True or False gives None (a bool is not a number of minutes).
  - An int or float is minutes: 30 gives 1800, 1.5 gives 90.
  - A string, stripped: a bare number (digits, optionally a dot and more digits) is minutes ("30" gives 1800); otherwise it is read as an ISO 8601 duration, case-insensitively: "PT1H30M" 5400, "pt15m" 900, "P1DT1H" 90000, "P1W" 604800, "PT1M1.53S" 62. Anything else gives None: "", "1 hour 30 minutes", "P1M" and "P1Y" (no fixed length), "PT-3H" (invalid).
  - A timedelta gives its length (timedelta(hours=1) gives 3600). A dict with "minValue" gives that value's result ({"minValue": "PT1H"} gives 3600). A non-empty list gives its first item's result (["PT1H", "PT2H"] gives 3600). None and anything else give None.
  - The result is rounded to the nearest second and must be above 0 and at most 2147483647, else None: 0, "PT0M", "PT" (a duration with no parts counts as zero), -5, "P30000D" and float("inf") all give None.
- clean_time(time_entry, translator) keeps writing durations as words with pretty_print_timedelta, with these rules (en-US translator):
  - None, "" and " " give None. Text that is not a duration is kept: "invalid" gives "invalid".
  - timedelta(minutes=30) gives "30 minutes"; "PT2H30M" "2 hours 30 minutes"; "PT30M" "30 minutes"; "PT2H" "2 hours"; "P1DT1H1M1S" and "P1DT1H1M1.53S" both "1 day 1 hour 1 minute 1 second" (fractions of a second are dropped); "P1D" "1 day"; "P3D" "3 days"; "P1W" "7 days".
  - Durations of zero or less give None, never "none": "PT", "PT0S", timedelta(0) and -5 (minutes).
  - ISO-looking text that is not a usable duration is kept exactly as given: "P1M" (months), "-PT1H" (negative) and "PT-3H".
- cleaner.clean(recipe_data, translator), for a dict or a Recipe, handles totalTime, prepTime and performTime this way: when the matching totalTimeSeconds, prepTimeSeconds or performTimeSeconds is missing or null and clean_duration reads the time, those seconds are stored and the text becomes null; otherwise the text is cleaned with clean_time as today. Seconds that are already set are kept as they are, and the text is still cleaned. {"name": "Test Recipe", "totalTime": "PT1H30M", "prepTime": 20, "performTime": "about an hour"} gives total_time_seconds 5400 and total_time None, prep_time_seconds 1200 and prep_time None, perform_time_seconds None and perform_time "about an hour". {"name": "Test Recipe", "totalTime": "PT2H", "totalTimeSeconds": 60} gives total_time_seconds 60 and total_time "2 hours".
- pretty_print_timedelta and the cleaner's other helpers (clean_string, clean_image, clean_instructions, clean_ingredients, clean_yield, clean_categories, clean_tags, clean_nutrition, clean_notes) keep their current behaviour, and clean still accepts the recipe JSON files in tests/data/json.

4. Scraping a URL: a recipe scraped from schema.org data (RecipeScraperPackage.clean_scraper followed by cleaner.clean, as the URL import does) gets structured times too, the perform time coming from performTime, else cookTime. ld+json with totalTime "PT1H30M", prepTime "PT20M" and cookTime "PT1H10M" ends with seconds 5400, 1200 and 4200 for total, prep and perform, and all three texts null. Times that are not durations stay text, and clean_scraper still keeps the schema.org notes.

5. Migrations from other apps (POST /api/groups/migrations) store structured times instead of English text. For the recipes below, the result is given as (total, prep, perform) seconds, and all three time texts are null:
- Nextcloud: totalTime, prepTime and cookTime in recipe.json are ISO durations for total, prep and perform. "Skillet Shepherd's Pie" (totalTime PT1H25M, prepTime PT0H15M, cookTime PT1H10M) gives (5100, 900, 4200).
- Tandoor: working_time and waiting_time are minutes; perform is working_time, total is working_time + waiting_time, there is no prep, and a zero time is null. "“Texas Red” Chili" (working_time 0, waiting_time 2) gives (120, None, None).
- My Recipe Box CSV: preparationTime, cookingTime and totalTime are minutes for prep, perform and total. "Beef & Cheese Piroshki" (preparationTime 90, cookingTime 25, totalTime 115) gives (6900, 5400, 1500); empty cells give nothing.
- Recipe Keeper: prepTime and cookTime are ISO durations for prep and perform; there is no total. "Zucchini Bread" (prepTime PT30M, cookTime PT1H) gives (None, 1800, 3600); "PT0S" gives nothing.
- Cook'n: PREPTIME and COOKTIME are minutes, for prep and perform, and total is their sum. "Fresh Fruit Pizza" (0 and 0) gives (None, None, None).
The rest of every migration is unchanged: each test archive (Paprika, Chowdown, Copy Me That, Mealie alpha and Plan to Eat too) still imports every entry successfully, with its timeline event, nutrition, categories, yield and notes; an upload Plan to Eat cannot read and an empty Mealie alpha recipe file are still reported as failures with the same messages.

6. AI import (POST /api/recipes/create/ai)
- The time fields of the AI recipe schema (OpenAIRecipe) ask the provider for an ISO 8601 duration (such as PT1H30M, PT30M or PT1H), or plain text when the time is not a clear duration (such as overnight). The built recipe is cleaned as in 3, so total_time "PT1H30M" is stored as totalTimeSeconds 5400 with totalTime null, and "overnight" stays text.
- With translateLanguage, the translation request carries only text: structured times are not sent ("PT1H30M" appears nowhere in that message), and the translated recipe keeps the built recipe's seconds, even though the provider's answer carries no time. Example: the build returns total_time "PT1H30M" and prep_time "overnight", the translation returns total_time null and prep_time "la nuit": exactly two recipe requests are made, the response is 201, and the stored recipe has totalTimeSeconds 5400, totalTime null, prepTimeSeconds null and prepTime "la nuit".
- Everything else in the AI import stays as it is (compiling sources, organizers, images, the translation as its own request carrying the whole recipe's text, skipping or surviving a translation, error messages and status codes, the streaming endpoint).

7. Recipe page metadata (schema.org)
- A new module-level function iso_duration(seconds) in the SPA module that serves recipe pages with metadata (the one with content_with_meta, inject_recipe_json and serve_recipe_with_meta). None or 0 give None; otherwise "PT" followed by hours with "H", minutes with "M" and seconds with "S", zero parts left out and no days: 45 gives "PT45S", 900 "PT15M", 5400 "PT1H30M", 3690 "PT1H1M30S", 93600 "PT26H".
- content_with_meta fills schema.org totalTime, prepTime and cookTime with iso_duration of total_time_seconds, prep_time_seconds and perform_time_seconds. Free text never goes there; without seconds the value is null. Example: total_time_seconds 5400, perform_time_seconds 3600, prep_time "a while" and cook_time "PT10M" give totalTime "PT1H30M", cookTime "PT1H" and prepTime null.
- Everything else is unchanged: the other schema.org fields and the meta tags, HTML escaping of recipe text, serving public and shared recipes, and the 404 for an unknown group or recipe, or for a private recipe or private group seen without a user.

8. Frontend
- A new composable module use-recipe-time in the recipes composables folder (the spec imports it as ../use-recipe-time from its __tests__ folder) exports three pure functions that take the locale as an argument and need no i18n setup. Unit names come from the platform's Intl unit formatting for that locale, not from the app's translation files.
  - formatDuration(seconds, locale): days, hours, minutes and seconds with the locale's long unit names, zero parts left out. In en-US: 60 gives "1 minute", 1800 "30 minutes", 3600 "1 hour", 5400 "1 hour 30 minutes", 90 "1 minute 30 seconds", 93600 "1 day 2 hours". In de-DE, 5400 starts with "1 Stunde" and ends with "30 Minuten" (how the parts are joined may vary).
  - durationUnitLabel(unit, locale), for unit "hour" or "minute": the locale's short unit name, "hr" and "min" in en-US.
  - recipeTimeDisplay(seconds, text, locale): the formatted duration (when seconds is set and not 0) followed by the trimmed text, joined by one space, empty parts left out. (10800, "plus overnight") gives "3 hours plus overnight"; (5400, null) and (5400, " ") give "1 hour 30 minutes"; (null, "overnight"), (undefined, "overnight") and (0, "overnight") give "overnight"; (null, null) and (null, "") give "".
- The recipe page, print view and recipe editor should show and edit the structured times next to the text, and the frontend API types get the three fields; that wiring is not graded.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests tests/integration_tests/test_spa.py tests/integration_tests/recipe_migration_tests tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

Frontend: `cd frontend && pnpm test:ci app/composables/recipes/__tests__/use-recipe-time.test.ts`.

feature-4a280cbd.text:
Feature: sign users in from a header set by a trusted reverse proxy.

Many self-hosters run Mealie behind a proxy that already authenticates people (Authelia, Authentik, oauth2-proxy, Tailscale Serve and similar) and passes the signed-in name on in a request header. Today those users still have to log in to Mealie a second time. Operators want an opt-in way, off by default, for Mealie to accept the forwarded name as a login. Password, LDAP and OIDC login must keep working as they do now.

Expected:

1. Settings. AppSettings gets five new settings, read from environment variables of the same names like the existing ones:
   - REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_ENABLED: a bool, default False.
   - REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_HEADER: a string, default "X-Forwarded-User". This header carries the username (or email).
   - REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED: a bool, default False. When true, unknown names are created as new users the first time they arrive.
   - REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SECRET: an optional string, unset (None) by default. When set, every request to the endpoint must carry it.
   - REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SECRET_HEADER: a string, default "X-Mealie-Reverse-Proxy-Secret". This header carries the secret.
   The settings class also gets REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_READY. Like OIDC_READY, it is a read-only Python property on the class, not a field. It is true only when the feature is enabled and a header name is configured.

2. A new public endpoint, GET /api/auth/reverse-proxy, sits beside POST /api/auth/token and needs no Mealie credentials:
   - When the feature is not ready (the default), it answers 404, even if the username header is present.
   - When a secret is configured and the secret header is missing or does not match it exactly, it answers 401. When no secret is configured, no secret header is needed.
   - When the username header is missing or empty, it answers 401.
   - Otherwise it authenticates through the provider in point 3. If no user results, it answers 401. On success it answers 200 with the same token body as POST /api/auth/token (access_token, token_type "bearer", expires_in) and sets the session cookie as the other logins do. The access_token works as a Bearer token: GET /api/users/self with it returns that user, with the same username.
   - The endpoint reads REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_READY, both header names and the secret from the module-level `settings` object of the module that holds the auth routes (get_token, oauth_native_token, refresh_token), as the OIDC endpoints there do. Changing an attribute on that object, or replacing the REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_READY property on its class, must change the endpoint's behaviour.

3. ReverseProxyProvider is a new subclass of AuthProvider, typed on str. It lives in a new module of the security providers package, mealie.core.security.providers (the package that holds auth_provider, credentials_provider, ldap_provider and openid_provider), and the module is named after the class the same way its siblings are named after theirs. It is constructed as ReverseProxyProvider(session, username), and authenticate() returns the (token, duration) pair like the other providers, or None:
   - For an empty username it returns None without using the session, which may be None.
   - For a user found by username or, failing that, by email (case-insensitive, as the other providers look users up), it returns a token.
   - For an unknown name with REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED true, it creates a non-admin user whose username and full name are the forwarded name, with auth method AuthMethod.REVERSE_PROXY. The name is also the email when it contains "@"; otherwise the user gets a unique placeholder email built from the name. It saves the user and returns a token. The new user is then found by repos.users.get_one(name, "username", any_case=True), and its auth_method is AuthMethod.REVERSE_PROXY.
   - For an unknown name with signup disabled (or when creating the user fails), it returns None and creates nothing.
   - The provider reads its settings from get_app_settings() each time it authenticates, so changing the environment and then clearing the get_app_settings cache (cache_clear) takes effect. It trusts the name it is given and does not itself check REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_ENABLED or REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_READY; the endpoint does that.

4. AuthMethod, the enum the User model uses (MEALIE, LDAP, OIDC), gains a member REVERSE_PROXY whose value is "ReverseProxy". As with LDAP and OIDC accounts, these users cannot log in with a password. On Postgres the auth method column uses the native enum type authmethod, so a new Alembic migration on top of the current head 3697d65c5f92 must add REVERSE_PROXY to that type. SQLite needs no schema change.

5. Status reporting: GET /api/app/about and GET /api/admin/about report enableReverseProxyAuth, which is true when the feature is ready. GET /api/admin/about/check reports reverseProxyAuthReady, and reverseProxyAuthDisabled, which is true when REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_ENABLED is false.

UI changes (the login page and admin site settings) are not part of this task.

feature-824265b3.text:
Feature: AI recipe import uses every source it is given, translates in its own step, and reports translated errors.

The AI import page posts to POST /api/recipes/create/ai, or to its SSE twin /api/recipes/create/ai/stream. The request is a multipart form with content, url, images, translateLanguage and createNewOrganizers. It has three problems today:
- Pasted content replaces the other sources instead of adding to them. With a URL, the page is not read at all. With images, the text is only passed along to the image reading and never reaches the recipe build as a source of its own.
- Translation is a clause prepended to the build request. That changes what the build step asks for, and it can make the provider invent a recipe.
- The failure message the page shows as-is is often an exception's own text or class name, which can expose provider internals, paths, or names like "RuntimeError".

Expected:

1. Every source is compiled and combined.
   - Images, the URL and the pasted content are each compiled on their own, by the same compilers as today, and the results are merged into the single compiled source document. The build, translation and organizer steps read that document.
   - The URL is downloaded as a video when it is one and an audio provider is set. Otherwise it is fetched as a page.
   - Pasted content is compiled exactly as when it is the only source. Plain text, schema.org JSON, and HTML that carries ld+json need no provider call, even when images or a URL are also given.
   - Images plus content: the provider gets one compile request for the images (response schema OpenAICompiledSource) and then the build request (OpenAIRecipe). The build request contains both the text compiled from the images and the pasted content.
   - URL plus content: the page is fetched once and compiled. The build request contains both what the page says (for example the name in its ld+json) and the pasted content. orgURL is the URL.
   - Video URL plus content: the build request contains the transcript and the pasted content. The video URL is never fetched as a webpage.
   - A video URL when no audio provider is set is fetched as a page, exactly once.
   - Pages are still fetched through the safe_scrape_html that the module defining CompileSourceStep imports today, called with the URL.
2. How the merged document is put together:
   - A single usable source is used as it is.
   - Several usable sources stay distinguishable in the merged document, with the user's pasted content last and authoritative where the sources disagree.
   - Their combined length is capped with truncate_source_parts (item 7), so a long page cannot crowd out pasted text.
   - The merged document keeps the first language and the first image URL the usable sources report. Uploaded images still take precedence as the recipe image.
   - A source is usable when it contains a recipe and its content is not blank.
   - If sources compiled but none is usable, the import answers 400 with recipe.import-errors.no-recipe-found. If nothing could be compiled at all, it answers recipe.import-errors.unreadable-source. An empty request is still a 400 (no-source).
3. HTML that the URL and HTML importers already hold. POST /api/recipes/create/url and POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json can fall back to the AI strategy (RecipeScraperOpenAI). The HTML that strategy has is that URL's own page, not extra pasted content.
   - The workflow must not fetch the URL again, and must not compile the same page twice.
   - Example: html-or-json with data and url answers 201 without fetching the page. The recipe has the provider's name, and orgURL is the url.
   - The rest keeps working as today:
     - URL import via AI, and html-or-json without url: 201, with the provider's name, ingredients and instructions.
     - An organizer request is made only when include_tags or include_categories asks for it. Tags are imported title-cased.
     - The html-or-json stream emits progress and done events.
     - 400 when the provider returns nothing, or when no default AI provider is set.
4. Translation is its own step.
   - The build request is identical whether or not translateLanguage is sent, and it never mentions the language.
   - After the recipe is built, and before organizers are resolved, a separate provider request translates the built recipe. It uses response schema OpenAIRecipe and a new stored system prompt of its own, kept alongside the existing recipe prompts and loaded with get_prompt.
   - The translation request's message contains the target language exactly as sent (for example "French"). It also contains the whole built recipe in the provider's recipe schema: name, description, yield and times, each ingredient's text and section title, each instruction's text and title, and each note's text and title.
   - The answer replaces the draft recipe. It is converted exactly as the build step's answer is (section titles, notes, image, orgURL, owner), keeps the untranslated recipe's nutrition, and is cleaned again. The saved recipe has the translated name.
   - With translation, the provider gets exactly two OpenAIRecipe requests: build, then translate.
   - There is no translation request when no language is asked for, or when the compiled source's language equals the requested one ignoring case. For example, a source in "French" with "french" requested is not translated.
   - The step is optional. If the translation request raises, or returns nothing, or returns a recipe with neither ingredients nor instructions, the untranslated recipe is saved: 201, with the original name.
   - The step reports progress with the key recipe.create-progress.translating-recipe. That key is the step's declared progress key in DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_STEPS, which now runs compile, build, translate, then organizers.
5. The error message is always translated.
   - This is the message the recipe-creation endpoints report for a failure: detail.message of the 400 from POST /api/recipes/create/ai, and the message of the stream's error event. It is always a translated string in the request's language.
   - It never contains the exception's own text or class name.
   - The mapping:
     - RateLimitError: the existing exceptions.rate-limit-error text, which mentions "rate limiting", as today.
     - NoRecipeDataError and AIProviderNotEnabledError: their own message, which is already translated, as today.
     - OpenAINotEnabledException (exported from the openai services package): recipe.import-errors.ai-not-enabled.
     - VideoDownloadError (mealie.core.exceptions): recipe.import-errors.video-download-failed, which is new.
     - OpenAIServiceError (mealie.core.exceptions): recipe.import-errors.ai-request-failed, which is new.
     - Scraper HTTPExceptions keep reporting their detail as today, for example the ParserErrors value BAD_RECIPE_DATA for the URL and HTML importers.
     - Anything else: recipe.import-errors.unknown-error, which is new.
   - Examples for a content import whose provider call raises:
     - OpenAIServiceError("Failed to transcribe audio: 401 invalid_api_key sk-proj-abc123") gives 400 with detail.message equal to the en-US text of recipe.import-errors.ai-request-failed.
     - VideoDownloadError(...) gives video-download-failed.
     - OpenAINotEnabledException("No default provider set") gives ai-not-enabled.
     - RuntimeError("psycopg2.OperationalError: ...") gives unknown-error.
6. Backend translations (the en-US backend messages that hold recipe.import-errors and recipe.create-progress).
   - Add four keys, each with a short user-facing en-US text:
     - recipe.import-errors.ai-request-failed: the AI provider could not complete the request; try again.
     - recipe.import-errors.unknown-error: something went wrong while creating the recipe; try again.
     - recipe.import-errors.video-download-failed: the video could not be downloaded; it may be private, removed or from an unsupported site.
     - recipe.create-progress.translating-recipe: "Translating recipe...".
   - Keep these consistency rules:
     - Every key under recipe.import-errors and recipe.create-progress is referenced somewhere in the backend Python code as a complete quoted string literal, such as "recipe.import-errors.unknown-error". Keys assembled at runtime do not count.
     - Every such literal resolves to an en-US translation.
     - Nothing is orphaned.
   - After the change, the referenced import-error keys are ai-not-enabled, ai-request-failed, image-provider-not-enabled, no-recipe-found, no-source, provider-returned-nothing, unknown-error, unreadable-source and video-download-failed.
   - The referenced progress keys are creating-recipe, creating-recipe-from-transcript-with-ai, creating-recipe-from-webpage-data, downloading-image, downloading-video, extracting-recipe-data, fetching-webpage, organizing-recipe, reading-images-with-ai, reading-source-with-ai, transcribing-audio-with-ai and translating-recipe.
   - The progress keys declared by DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_STEPS and DEFAULT_SOURCE_COMPILERS stay as they are, plus the new one, each declared once:
     - creating-recipe (build) and organizing-recipe (organizers);
     - reading-images-with-ai, downloading-video and reading-source-with-ai (compilers);
     - translating-recipe (the new translation step).
7. A new function truncate_source_parts(parts, max_length=MAX_SOURCE_CONTENT_LENGTH) returns a list of strings. It goes next to truncate_source_content, in the module that holds it along with MAX_SOURCE_CONTENT_LENGTH and TRUNCATION_NOTICE.
   - It caps a group of texts so that their combined length fits max_length, and returns them in input order.
   - Every part gets an equal integer share of the budget.
   - A part shorter than its share keeps its full text, and what it leaves unused is shared among the longer parts.
   - A part longer than its final allowance is cut like truncate_source_content: its first allowance characters plus TRUNCATION_NOTICE. The notice is not counted against the budget.
   - Examples:
     - ["a"*10, "b"*10] with 100 is unchanged.
     - ["a"*100, "b"*100] with 10 gives ["a"*5 + notice, "b"*5 + notice].
     - ["a"*1000, "b"*10] with 100 gives ["a"*90 + notice, "b"*10].
     - [] gives [].
   - truncate_source_content itself does not change. Content up to the limit is untouched; longer content is cut to max_length plus the notice; a custom max_length works.
8. These existing POST /api/recipes/create/ai behaviours must keep working:
   - Content-only plain text, and schema.org JSON, make no OpenAICompiledSource request.
   - Images get a compile request and then a build request, and the first image is saved as the recipe's original.webp.
   - A URL whose page carries ld+json gives 201, with the provider's name and orgURL set to the URL.
   - A video URL with an audio provider is transcribed, never fetched as a page, and needs no compile request.
   - Organizers:
     - There is no organizer request when the group has none and createNewOrganizers is off.
     - Existing organizers are attached and unknown names are dropped; nothing is created.
     - New organizers are created when createNewOrganizers is "true".
     - The organizer request reads the compiled source, so a "tags: ..." line in pasted text reaches it.
     - The group's existing tags are listed in the organizer prompt.
     - An organizer failure does not lose the recipe.
   - The no-image placeholder is never downloaded, and never stored as the image.
   - A RateLimitError gives 400 mentioning "rate limiting".
   - Section titles and nutrition survive: ingredient titles are "For the sauce" and null, step titles are "Prep" and "", and calories "250" with proteinContent "12" (from "12 g").
   - 400 for: no source; a source with no recipe (contains_recipe false); a provider that returns nothing; no default AI provider; images without an image provider.
   - The stream answers 200 with progress and done events, or ends with an error event.

The UI text changes from the original change (hints on the AI import page) are not part of this task.

feature-97a66c19.text:
Feature: recipe counts, "unused" lists and merging for foods, tools and labels.

Tags and categories already report how many recipes use them, can list their unused entries (GET .../empty) and can be merged into one another (POST .../merge). Group organizers want the same clean-up tools for foods, tools and labels: see how many recipes use each one, find the ones nothing uses, and fold duplicates together. While doing this we also noticed that the existing tag and category "empty" lists return unused tags and categories from every group, not only the caller's, so a "delete unused" action built on them would reach into other groups.

Expected (paths under /api, JSON in camelCase):

Recipe counts
1. Foods get a recipeCount field (recipe_count in Python): the number of distinct recipes that have at least one ingredient line using the food. It appears on each item of GET /api/foods and on GET /api/foods/{id}, and is 0 for a food no recipe uses. It defaults to 0 wherever no count is loaded, so building an IngredientFood from an object that carries no count still validates. A food object exactly as the API returns it (now with recipeCount) can be sent back inside a recipe's recipeIngredient in PUT /api/recipes/{slug}, which still answers 200.
2. Tools: the recipeCount already present on items of GET /api/organizers/tools (today always 0) becomes the number of recipes that have the tool. An unused tool still shows 0.

Unused lists. Each answers 200 with a plain JSON list (not paginated) of entries from the caller's group only; an unused entry of another group never appears.
3. GET /api/foods/empty: foods referenced by no recipe ingredient and by no shopping-list item. A food that no recipe uses but that is still on a shopping-list item is not listed (deleting it would break that item).
4. GET /api/organizers/tools/empty: tools attached to no recipe.
5. GET /api/groups/labels/empty: labels referenced by no food and by no shopping-list item. The per-shopping-list label settings (one row per group label, created automatically with each list) do not count as use.
6. GET /api/organizers/tags/empty and GET /api/organizers/categories/empty keep working as now, but are limited to the caller's group in the same way.

Merging
7. New POST /api/organizers/tools/merge and POST /api/groups/labels/merge take the body {"fromId": <uuid>, "toId": <uuid>} and behave like the existing tag and category merge endpoints: only a user with the organize permission may call them; 400 when fromId equals toId; 404 (not 500) when fromId or toId is not a tool, or label, of the caller's group; otherwise 200 with the target object (its id is toId), and the fromId object is deleted.
   - Tools: every recipe that had the merged-away tool now has the target tool, once, and no recipe keeps the merged-away one. A recipe that already had both must not cause a unique-constraint error; it ends with just the target. The returned tool's recipeCount is counted after the merge: merging a tool used by one recipe into a tool used by another recipe gives 2; when a single recipe had both, it gives 1. GET /api/organizers/tools/{fromId} then answers 404.
   - Labels: foods and shopping-list items that pointed at the merged-away label now point at the target (GET /api/foods/{id} shows label.id equal to toId; GET /api/households/shopping/items/{id} shows labelId equal to toId). Every shopping list's labelSettings ends with exactly one entry for the target label and none for the merged-away label, including lists that already had a settings row for both. The merged-away label no longer appears in GET /api/groups/labels.
8. The existing PUT /api/foods/merge (body {"fromFood", "toFood"}) keeps working as today (200, GET /api/foods/{fromFood} then answers 404, recipes that used it now reference the target), and GET /api/foods/{toFood} then reports the combined count: 2 when each food was used by one different recipe.

Must keep working:
- Creating a tool (POST /api/organizers/tools, 201) or a label (POST /api/groups/labels, 200) stays open to any member of the group, including a user without the organize permission, as today.
- The group-scoped repositories (get_repositories(session, group_id=..., household_id=...)) still create and delete foods, tags and categories directly: repos.ingredient_foods.create(SaveIngredientFood(name=..., group_id=...)), repos.tags.create(TagSave(...)) and repos.categories.create(CategorySave(...)) return an object with an id, and .delete(id) removes it.
- Tag and category recipe counts and merges, tool create/read/update/delete and lookup by slug, and recipe-tool associations behave as before.
- The route constants module tests/utils/api_routes (generated from the app's routes) gains foods_empty, groups_labels_empty, groups_labels_merge, organizers_tools_empty and organizers_tools_merge for the new paths.

The frontend data-management pages (delete-unused and merge dialogs) are not part of this task.

feature-a1a49d22.text:
Feature: keep sessions alive with token refresh, make "Remember me" decide whether the session survives closing the browser, and stop Safari from cutting sessions to seven days.

Several login-session problems, reported together:
- The SPA writes the session cookie (mealie.access_token) itself through document.cookie. Safari caps every cookie written by script at seven days, so iOS users are signed out after a week whatever TOKEN_TIME says.
- Nothing ever refreshes a session. When the token runs out mid-edit, the next request answers 401 and the user is thrown to /login.
- "Remember me" only stretches the token to at least 14 days, which does nothing when TOKEN_TIME is longer, and an unticked box still leaves a cookie that survives closing the browser.
- Changing your password does not sign out anyone who already holds a session token.
- The refresh endpoint (GET /api/auth/refresh) will trade a long-lived API token for a session token, which then outlives the API token's revocation.

Expected, backend:

1. Tokens. create_access_token(data, expires_delta=None), importable from the mealie.core.security package, returns a pair (token, lifetime): the signed JWT and the timedelta it was granted, which is TOKEN_TIME hours by default or expires_delta when given (timedelta(minutes=5) gives 5 minutes). Every token it signs (session, API and file tokens alike) carries the given claims plus iss equal to ISS ("mealie") and an iat issue time, and exp minus iat is exactly the lifetime in seconds. ISS and ALGORITHM ("HS256") are importable from mealie.core.security too, next to the names it already exports (create_file_token, get_auth_provider, hash_password, url_safe_token and so on). create_file_token(path) still returns only the token string, and validate_file_token still turns it back into the path. Creating an API token (POST /api/users/api-tokens, 201 with the token string), using it and deleting it keep working.
2. validate_file_token answers a correctly signed token that has no file claim (a session token, for example) with HTTPException 401 instead of failing with a 500.
3. Login, POST /api/auth/token. The JSON body is access_token, token_type "bearer" and a new integer expires_in, the token lifetime in seconds (TOKEN_TIME x 3600). The remember_me form field (true or false, default false) no longer changes the lifetime: every session token lasts exactly TOKEN_TIME. The choice is recorded on the token as a boolean claim rme (true or false). A wrong password still gets 401, and a locked-out user 423.
4. The server sets the session cookie. A successful login sends a Set-Cookie header (the first one in the response) that starts with mealie.access_token=<the access token> and has Path=/. When remember_me is true it has a Max-Age equal to the lifetime in seconds; when false it has no Max-Age, so it ends with the browser session. The cookie stays readable by page scripts (not HttpOnly), because the SPA reads it to build its Authorization header. The OIDC logins (the callback and the native token exchange) answer the same body, expires_in included, and set the same cookie, persistent when OIDC_REMEMBER_ME is true.
   Its other attributes come from a new function session_cookie_attrs(request) in the auth routes module (the one that defines get_token and MealieAuthToken). It returns a dict that includes "secure" (bool), "samesite" ("lax" or "none") and "partitioned" (bool):
   - secure is True when the request scheme is https, or when the first comma-separated entry of the X-Forwarded-Proto header is https (trimmed), even when the proxy is not trusted: "https" and "https, http" give True, "http, https" gives False, and plain http without the header gives False.
   - When secure is True and the request carries the header X-Mealie-Embedded: true, samesite is "none" and partitioned is True; that includes an http-scheme request with X-Forwarded-Proto: https. Otherwise samesite is "lax" and partitioned is False, so X-Mealie-Embedded: true over plain http stays "lax" and False.
   Setting and clearing the cookie use the same attributes.
5. Refresh becomes POST /api/auth/refresh (no longer GET). It needs a valid credential and answers 401 to an invalid bearer token or to none at all. It answers like login (token_type "bearer", expires_in = TOKEN_TIME x 3600) with a new session token for the same user that works on GET /api/users/self (same id). The new token keeps the rme value of the token the call was made with (true stays true, false stays false), and the response sends the session cookie again with the new token (with Max-Age when rme is true). A long-lived API token is refused with 400.
6. Logout, POST /api/auth/logout, clears the cookie: its Set-Cookie starts with mealie.access_token= and contains Max-Age=0, with the same attributes the cookie was set with. The response body does not change.
7. Token lookup. A new async dependency get_auth_token(request, token) in the dependencies module that defines get_current_user and validate_file_token. token is the Authorization bearer token as the existing soft-fail OAuth2 scheme yields it (None when absent). It returns that token when one was sent, even if a mealie.access_token cookie is present too; otherwise the value of the mealie.access_token cookie; otherwise "" (other cookies are ignored). The current user is resolved from that token, so requests keep authenticating with the header first and the cookie as fallback.
8. A password change ends existing sessions. Every password change (PUT /api/users/password, the password-reset flow, the change-password script) records its time on the user, in a new nullable NaiveDateTime column tokens_valid_after on users, added by a new Alembic migration revising 2187537c52b8 (it becomes the only head; name its file with the project's migration template so it sorts after the existing ones). From then on a session token issued before the change gets 401 (on GET /api/users/self, for example), and so does a token without iat. Issue times are whole seconds, so compare at whole-second precision: a token issued in the same second as the change, or later, keeps working, and logging in with the new password right after the change gives a working token. Long-lived API tokens are not affected: one created before the change still gets 200.
9. API token ownership. DELETE /api/users/api-tokens/{id} by another user of the same group answers 403 and leaves the token in place; its owner can still delete it (200). Ownership is checked by user id.
10. Backups. A restore turns values back into datetimes only for the column names listed in AlchemyExporter.look_for_datetime, so every column of type NaiveDateTime in the models' metadata must be listed there. completed_date is missing today, and the new column must be listed too. The dump's alembic_version must still equal the revision of the newest migration file, and the dump must stay JSON-serializable.

Expected, frontend:

11. In the module that exports getTokenCookieOptions:
   - getTokenCookieOptions() returns no maxAge key at all (the server owns the cookie's lifetime). The rest is unchanged: secure is true only for a production build ($appInfo.production) on an https: page; sameSite is "none" and partitioned true only when that page is also framed (window.self !== window.top); otherwise "lax" and false.
   - New getTokenExpiry(token): the JWT payload's exp in epoch milliseconds, decoding base64url with or without padding (exp 1 gives 1000, exp 12 gives 12000). It returns null for a payload without exp, and returns null rather than throwing for "not-a-jwt", "header.@@@notbase64@@@.signature" and "".
   - New readTokenCookie(name): the URL-decoded value of exactly that cookie in document.cookie (a value written as encodeURIComponent("a.b+c/d") reads back as "a.b+c/d"), or null when that cookie is absent, even if other cookies are set.
   - New nextRefreshDelay(remainingMs, jitter): the milliseconds to wait before refreshing a token with remainingMs left to live; jitter is a number from 0 to 1 and defaults to a random one. The delay is 60% of remainingMs but at least 30000, plus jitter x 30000, and the total is capped at 2^31 - 1 = 2147483647. So (10 h, 0) gives 6 h; (10000, 0) gives 30000; (10 h, 1) and (10 h, 0.5) give 6 h + 30000 and 6 h + 15000; (400 days, 0) gives 2147483647; with jitter 1 the result never exceeds the cap (42 days, 400 days, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). It returns null when remainingMs is 0 or less.
12. useAuthBackend():
   - The client stops writing the token cookie; it only ever clears it. setToken(token) keeps the token in memory, shared by every useAuthBackend() caller: auth.token shows it at once, and a background refresh is scheduled from its exp. setToken(null) clears the in-memory token, the scheduled refresh and the cookie, and auth.token becomes null.
   - refresh() resolves without any request when there is neither an in-memory token nor a token cookie. Otherwise it calls $axios.post once with the URL "/api/auth/refresh", a null body and the config { suppressAlert: true } (exactly that object). Calls made while one is in flight share it: three concurrent calls make one POST and all resolve. Once it settles, the next call makes a new request, after a failure too (two failing calls make two POSTs, and both reject with the error). On success it adopts response.data.access_token as the token and does nothing more; in particular it does not call GET /api/users/self. On a 401 it clears the token (null), calls router.push("/login") and rejects. On any other error (a network failure, say) it rejects but keeps the token and does not navigate.
   - signIn(formData) posts the credentials as today and keeps data.access_token as the token; then getSession() calls $axios.get("/api/users/self") (with that single argument) and status becomes "authenticated". getSession must see the token signIn just set, although the client never wrote the cookie. When the credentials are rejected, signIn rethrows, status is "unauthenticated" and no GET is made.
   - signOut(callbackUrl) clears the token and the cookie and navigates to callbackUrl, or to "/login" without one (signOut("/recipes") goes to "/recipes"), even when POST /api/auth/logout fails with a 401.
   The spec stubs useNuxtApp ($axios with get and post, $appInfo), useRouter, useRuntimeConfig (public.AUTH_TOKEN = "mealie.access_token"), clearNuxtData and useCookie (a minimal object whose value reads and writes document.cookie), mocks the store and composable-cache modules, and imports the module afresh for each test.
13. The Nuxt axios plugin (the one that creates the shared axios instance and its interceptors):
   - Every request reads the token from document.cookie when it is sent and sets Authorization: Bearer <token>. When the page is framed (window.self !== window.top) it also sets the header X-Mealie-Embedded to "true", since the server cannot detect embedding itself.
   - A 401 while a token cookie is present calls useAuthBackend().refresh() and then replays the original request once, with the token the cookie holds after the refresh. If the replay succeeds the caller gets its response and nothing redirects. Only one replay per request: an endpoint that always answers 401 causes a single refresh, then the request rejects.
   - If the refresh fails, or the replay gets 401 again, the session ends as today: useAuthBackend().setToken(null), then window.location.href = "/login?redirect=" followed by the URL-encoded path and query (on /g/home/r/soup that is "/login?redirect=%2Fg%2Fhome%2Fr%2Fsoup"). Any other error on the replay rejects as itself.
   - A 401 from /api/auth/token or /api/auth/refresh never triggers a refresh. A 401 from /api/auth/logout triggers neither a refresh nor the redirect (signOut navigates by itself). Without a token cookie a 401 simply rejects: no refresh, no redirect.
   The spec provides only defineNuxtPlugin, useRuntimeConfig and useAuthBackend (returning refresh and setToken) as globals, not useCookie or useNuxtApp. It calls the plugin's setup function with an app object that only has runWithContext(fn), and swaps the adapter of the axios instance the plugin provides. So the plugin must reach the composable through the auto-imported useAuthBackend (an explicit import would bypass the stub) and read the cookie directly.

The remaining UI wiring is not graded: starting the background refresh when the app boots (re-scheduling it on focus, visibility and reconnect, and following token changes made in other tabs), pages that called refresh() only to reload the user calling getSession() instead, the login form's Remember me ticked by default, and the profile page signing out after a password change.

feature-b386e728.text:
Feature: link recipe notes to instruction steps.

A step can already point at the ingredients it uses (ingredientReferences). Cooks want the same for notes: a step should be able to point at one or more of the recipe's notes (for example "see the note on resting the dough"), and the links should survive saving and loading the recipe.

Expected:
1. Every recipe note has a stable identifier. RecipeNote (title, text) gains reference_id (referenceId in JSON), a UUID. A note built or sent without one (missing, null or empty) gets a new random UUID, so RecipeNote(title=..., text=...) already has one, and every note of a recipe read back after it is created has a non-None reference_id. A note sent with a reference_id keeps it: it is stored with the note and returned unchanged by later reads and updates, so links to it stay valid. Clients that send notes with only title and text keep working; their notes get ids.
2. A new model NoteReference, importable from the same module as RecipeStep (next to IngredientReferences), with a single field reference_id (referenceId in JSON), an optional UUID that defaults to None.
3. RecipeStep gains note_references (noteReferences in JSON): a list of NoteReference, empty by default. RecipeStep(text="step one", note_references=[]) is valid.
4. The recipe repository stores a step's note references and loads them back. For example: create a recipe through a user's repositories (repos.recipes.create) with notes=[RecipeNote(title="my note", text="note body")] and one step RecipeStep(text="step one", note_references=[]); read reference_id from the returned recipe's first note; set the returned recipe's first step's note_references to [NoteReference(reference_id=<that id>)] and call repos.recipes.update(recipe.slug, recipe). The recipe it returns has exactly one note reference on its first step, and that reference's reference_id equals the note's reference_id (as a UUID). Through the API, GET /api/recipes/{slug} returns each note with its referenceId and each step with noteReferences ([{"referenceId": ...}]), and PUT /api/recipes/{slug} stores them.
5. When a recipe is updated through the API (PUT /api/recipes/{slug}), a step's note reference whose id matches none of the recipe's notes after the update is dropped, the same way references to removed ingredients are dropped today.
6. A new Alembic migration, revising the current head 4b91d3a7c0e2 and so becoming the only head, adds the storage this needs and gives every existing note a fresh reference id. Its file is named by the project's migration file template with a create date later than the newest existing migration's, so the files still sort in revision order. Downgrade removes what it added.

Showing and choosing linked notes in the recipe editor and on the recipe page is UI work and not part of this task.

feature-bf16ca15.text:
Feature: subscribe to the household meal plan as an iCal calendar feed.

People plan meals in Mealie but live in their calendar app (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, Outlook). They want to add the household's plan to that app by URL so planned meals show up there and stay current. Calendar apps poll a URL without logging in, so the feed has to be public but guarded by a secret token that a household manager can turn on, replace and turn off.

Expected:

1. Feed token management, for logged-in users and always about their own household, at /api/households/mealplans/ical:
   - GET answers 200 with a JSON object whose mealplanIcalToken is the household's current token, or null when the feed is off (it may also carry householdId). The feed is off by default, for new and existing households. Any member of the household may read the token, including a user without can_manage_household.
   - POST answers 200 (not 201). It turns the feed on with a new random, URL-safe secret token and returns the same object with that token (a non-empty string). Calling it again replaces the token with a different one, and the old token stops working at once.
   - DELETE answers 200. It turns the feed off and returns the object with mealplanIcalToken null; the previous token stops working.
   - POST and DELETE need the can_manage_household permission. A user without it gets 403 and the current token keeps working.
   - The token belongs to the household and must be unique. Storing it is a database change, so add a new Alembic migration revising the current head f3a8b6c1d2e4 (no test depends on the new revision id). The existing migration tests (tests/unit_tests/test_alembic.py and tests/unit_tests/services_tests/backup_v2_tests/test_alchemy_exporter.py) expect the migration files, sorted by file name, to form one chain that ends at the head, so the new file must sort last; the project's date-based file name template does that for a create date after 2026-10-14.
   - The token is a secret. It must not appear anywhere in the responses of GET /api/households/self or GET /api/households/preferences. Updating preferences with PUT /api/households/preferences (a full preferences body, for example the defaults with firstDayOfWeek 1) still answers 200 and leaves the token, and the feed, working.
   - The existing meal plan routes and GET /openapi.json keep working.

2. The feed: GET /api/households/mealplans/ical/{token}, with no authentication at all (no header, no cookie).
   - A token that matches no household (for example a random 32-character string), a replaced token, or the token of a feed that was turned off answers 404.
   - A valid token answers 200 with a Content-Type of text/calendar (a charset parameter is fine) and an RFC 5545 calendar of that household's meal plan entries only. Entries of other households, whether in the same group or another group, never appear.
   - Optional query parameters, camelCase like the rest of the API:
     - types: a meal type to include, repeatable (types=dinner&types=lunch). Values are the PlanEntryType values breakfast, lunch, dinner, side, snack, drink and dessert. Missing or empty means every type. An unknown value such as brunch answers 422.
     - includeNotes: a boolean, default true. With false, entries without a recipe (notes, which only have a title) are left out.
     - tz: an IANA time zone name such as Europe/Berlin, used for timed events. It defaults to the server's local time zone. An unknown zone such as Not/AZone answers 422.
     - A start time for each meal type, in a parameter named after the type: breakfast, lunch, dinner, side, snack, drink and dessert, each a time of day such as 18:30. Entries of a type that has a start time become timed events of one hour, starting at that time on the entry's date in tz. Entries of the other types are all-day events.
   - History: entries dated more than FEED_HISTORY_DAYS (90) days before today, where today is the current UTC date, are left out. The boundary is inclusive: an entry dated exactly 90 days ago is in the feed, one dated 91 days ago is not. Entries for today and later are always in the feed.

3. Feed format. Every line ends with CRLF, the last one included.
   - The body starts with the line BEGIN:VCALENDAR and ends with the line END:VCALENDAR (then CRLF). It carries the usual calendar properties: VERSION:2.0 and a PRODID, and may add CALSCALE:GREGORIAN, METHOD:PUBLISH and an X-WR-CALNAME naming the household.
   - One event per included entry, from a BEGIN:VEVENT line to an END:VEVENT line, with:
     - a UID that is unique and stable for the entry, and a DTSTAMP in UTC (YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ).
     - For an all-day event, the line DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD (the entry's date) directly followed by the line DTEND;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD with the next day's date.
     - For a timed event, the line DTSTART:YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ directly followed by DTEND:YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ one hour later, both converted to UTC. Example: a dinner entry on July 1 with dinner=18:30 and tz=Europe/Berlin (UTC+2 in July) gives DTSTART:<year>0701T163000Z then DTEND:<year>0701T173000Z, while a breakfast entry the same day with no breakfast time stays DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:<year>0701.
     - SUMMARY:<Type>: <title>. <Type> is the meal type's name with its first letter in upper case: in English Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Side, Snack, Drink, Dessert (the backend's existing mealplan.entry-type.<type> translations hold these names). <title> is the recipe's name when the entry has a recipe, otherwise the entry's title. The whole value is escaped as an RFC 5545 TEXT value (rules in 4). So a dinner entry for the recipe "Pasta" gives the line SUMMARY:Dinner: Pasta, and a lunch note titled "Leftovers, again; sorry" gives the line SUMMARY:Lunch: Leftovers\, again\; sorry
     - For an entry with a recipe, URL:<BASE_URL>/g/<group slug>/r/<recipe slug>, where BASE_URL is the app setting (the recipe page link the app already puts in its event notifications), not escaped.
     - Optionally a DESCRIPTION (escaped) with the entry's text and the recipe link.
   - Long lines are folded as RFC 5545 asks: every physical line (the body split on CRLF) is at most 75 octets in UTF-8, and each continuation line starts with a single space. Removing every CRLF followed by a space gives back the unfolded lines above.

4. These live in a new service module importable as mealie.services.household_services.mealplan_ical_service (in the package that already holds HouseholdService):
   - FEED_HISTORY_DAYS, a module-level int equal to 90, used for the history window above.
   - _escape_text(value: str) -> str escapes a TEXT value. Each backslash becomes two backslashes, a semicolon becomes \; and a comma becomes \, and every line break (CRLF, a lone LF or a lone CR) becomes the two characters \n. Colons are left alone. For example a\b;c,d followed by CRLF, then e, LF, f becomes a\\b\;c\,d\ne\nf.
   - _fold(line: str) -> str folds one content line, given without its line ending, and returns it without a trailing CRLF. A line of at most 75 UTF-8 octets comes back unchanged (for example SUMMARY:Dinner). A longer line comes back as pieces joined by CRLF plus a single space, where each piece, counting the leading space of the continuation pieces, is at most 75 octets. Breaks fall only between characters, never inside a multi-byte character such as an emoji or ä, and removing every CRLF plus space gives the original line back.

No new third-party package is needed. The upstream change also adds a meal planner dialog for the feed; UI changes are not part of this task.

feature-e3cf55b9.text:
Feature: show how many recipes use each tag and category, and merge one tag or category into another.

Group members who tidy their organizers cannot see how many recipes use a tag or a category. To fold a duplicate into another (say "Veggie" into "Vegetarian"), they have to re-tag every recipe by hand and then delete the old one.

Expected:

1. Recipe counts.
   - GET /api/organizers/tags and GET /api/organizers/categories add recipeCount (recipe_count) to every entry in items.
   - recipeCount is the number of recipes carrying that tag or category. It is 0 for an unused one, and 1 after a single recipe has been given it with PUT /api/recipes/{slug}.
   - The other fields stay as they are.
2. Merge endpoints: POST /api/organizers/tags/merge and POST /api/organizers/categories/merge.
   - The JSON body is {"fromId": "<uuid>", "toId": "<uuid>"} (fields from_id and to_id, with the usual camelCase aliases).
   - They need the same organizer permission as creating, updating or deleting organizers.
   - fromId equal to toId answers 400.
   - A fromId (or toId) that is not an organizer of the user's group answers 404, for example a random UUID.
   - Otherwise every recipe that carried the "from" organizer ends up carrying the "to" organizer instead.
   - A recipe that already carried both keeps a single link to "to". The merge must not hit the unique constraint on the recipe/organizer link table, and must not leave duplicates.
   - Then the "from" organizer is deleted, so GET /api/organizers/tags/{fromId} (or /categories/{fromId}) answers 404.
   - The changes are applied together: if anything fails, nothing is changed.
3. The merge response.
   - It answers 200 with the surviving organizer as JSON: its id (equal to toId), name, slug, groupId, and its recipeCount after the merge.
   - Example: "from" on one recipe and "to" on another gives recipeCount 2, and both recipes now list only "to".
   - Example: a single recipe carrying both gives recipeCount 1, and that recipe lists "to" but not "from".

Only tags and categories are in scope. The UI parts of the original change (showing the counts, a merge dialog, deleting unused organizers) are not part of this task.

fix-30ba9a65.text:
Bug: recipe pictures disappear after an edit, and recipes without a picture keep asking for one that 404s.

The frontend decides whether a recipe has a picture from the recipe's image value (the cache key stored in recipes.image): empty means no picture (it shows the placeholder and requests nothing), anything else means it requests the picture from /api/media/recipes/{id}/images/.... That value has drifted out of sync with the files on disk, in both directions:

1. Edits clear it. Upload a picture with PUT /api/recipes/{slug}/image (form field extension "jpg", file field image); it answers 200 with a non-empty image key. Then GET /api/recipes/{slug}, remove the image key from the JSON and PUT the rest back to /api/recipes/{slug}. The update answers 200, but the recipe's image is now null, although GET /api/media/recipes/{id}/images/original.webp still serves the file. The picture vanishes from the UI.
2. Scraping sets it regardless. finalize_scraped_recipe(recipe, translator), the step create_from_html uses to finish a scraped recipe, gives the recipe a fresh cache key whether or not an image was downloaded: also when there is no image URL, when the image is the placeholder "no image", and when the download produced nothing. When the download raises, it stores "no image", which also reads as "has a picture". Every render of such a recipe then requests a file that 404s.

Expected:
- A PUT /api/recipes/{slug} whose body has no image key answers 200 and keeps the stored image: a later GET returns exactly the key the upload returned, and GET /api/media/recipes/{id}/images/original.webp still answers 200. An explicit "image": null still clears it (GET then returns null), and an explicit value is still stored as given.
- RecipeDataService.scrape_image(image_url) returns the Path of the image file it wrote, or None when nothing was downloaded (the request failed or gave no usable response). It still raises, as today, for non-image content and for input it cannot read a URL from.
- finalize_scraped_recipe downloads through RecipeDataService.scrape_image (on a RecipeDataService for the recipe, called with just the image URL) and leaves a fresh non-empty cache key in image only when that call returned a path. In every other case image ends up empty (None): when the call returned None, when the image is None or "no image" (no download is attempted for those), and when the download raised. Name and slug handling stay as they are.
- The same rule applies wherever an image is fetched: POST /api/recipes/{slug}/image with a URL whose download yields no file answers 400 with an ErrorResponse saying the image could not be downloaded, and leaves the recipe's image as it was; recipes created by the data migrations (importers) never keep the source's image reference (an archive path or a URL) as their image value, and get a cache key only once their image file has been written.
- Existing installs are repaired once by a new Alembic migration with revision id 4b91d3a7c0e2, revising f2191b69db2e (the current head), so it becomes the only head. Its file is named by the project's migration file template (so the name carries the revision id), with a create date later than the newest existing migration's, so the files still sort in revision order. Upgrade: a recipe whose folder holds images/original.webp but whose image is empty or "no image" gets a new cache key; a recipe whose image is set but which has no such file gets NULL. If some recipes reference an image but no recipe has an image file at all (for example, the data volume is not mounted), nothing is cleared; only the repairs are made. Downgrade does nothing.
- That migration module can be imported on its own, outside an Alembic run, and has a module-level function _image_on_disk that takes two positional arguments, the recipe data directory (a Path) and a recipe id, and returns a bool. It is True exactly when <data directory>/<recipe id as a dashed UUID string>/images/original.webp is a file. The id may arrive as a uuid.UUID (Postgres), as the dashed string, or as the 32-character undashed hex string SQLite stores; all three find the same file. It is False when the recipe's images folder exists without original.webp (for a UUID and for the undashed hex alike). It only looks and creates no folders.
